title: Artinian lifting with finite-type bottom maps detects scheme smoothness
statement: Let $f:W\to V$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $V$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. A local ring has a unique maximal ideal; an Artinian ring satisfies the descending chain condition on ideals. A small extension $\varphi:B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ means a surjection of Artinian local commutative rings whose kernel $I$ is square zero and has length one as a $B'$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Put $i=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}B'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose that for every small extension and every commutative square given by $b:\operatorname{Spec}B\to W$ and $c:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to V$ with $fb=ci$ and with $c$ of finite type, there exists $b':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to W$ such that $b'i=b$ and $fb'=c$. Then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. No residue-field, separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 02HY (lemma-lifting-along-artinian), implication (2) to (1). The square-zero condition in the definition of small extension is redundant and is made explicit for its subsequent use.

proof.text: Fix a finite type point $w\in W$, so the canonical map $p:\operatorname{Spec}k\to W$, $k=\kappa(w)$, is finite type. For any affine open $D=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V$ containing $f(w)$, choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq f^{-1}(D)$ containing $w$. Factor $p$ through $U$. The affine-pairs criterion applied to $f$ and to $p$ shows that $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra and $k$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra. Explicitly, if $A=R[a_1,\ldots,a_r]$ and $k=A[t_1,\ldots,t_s]$ under the induced maps, then $k=R[\bar a_1,\ldots,\bar a_r,t_1,\ldots,t_s]$. Thus the canonical composite $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$ has finitely generated coordinate algebra over every such $D$.

source.place: Tag 02HY (lemma-lifting-along-artinian), implication (2) to (1). The square-zero condition in the definition of small extension is redundant and is made explicit for its subsequent use.

proof.text: Consider a test square for the fixed-residue criterion at $w$: a small extension $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$ with residue fields identified with $k$, a map $b:\operatorname{Spec}B\to W$ restricting to $p$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $c:\operatorname{Spec}B'\to V$ with $fb=ci$. Both Artinian spectra have one point, so $c$ maps that point to $f(w)$. For each affine open $D=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V$ containing $f(w)$, factor $c$ through $D$. Its residue map is the canonical composite of step 1, hence $k$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra. The Artinian finite-type residue criterion gives that $B'$ is finitely generated over $R$. For an affine open of $V$ not containing $f(w)$ the preimage is empty. These computations establish local finite type from its affine-cover definition. Every inverse image is empty or the one-point space $\operatorname{Spec}B'$, hence quasi-compact. Thus $c$ is finite type, as required by the hypothesis of the item.

source.place: Tag 02HY (lemma-lifting-along-artinian), implication (2) to (1). The square-zero condition in the definition of small extension is redundant and is made explicit for its subsequent use.

proof.text: The fixed-residue criterion defines small extensions by length one. This also gives the square-zero condition required here: the nonzero kernel $I$ is simple, since an intermediate nonzero proper submodule would give a chain of length two. Any nonzero generator identifies $I$ with $B'/\mathfrak m_{B'}$: its annihilator is maximal and the ring is local. Hence $\mathfrak m_{B'}I=0$; since the proper ideal $I$ lies in $\mathfrak m_{B'}$, $I^2=0$. By step 2 the bottom map $c$ is finite type. The assumed lifting property therefore supplies the lift for every fixed-residue test square at $w$. Apply the fixed-residue Artinian criterion to $f$, which is locally finite type with locally Noetherian target, to obtain an open neighbourhood $N_w$ of $w$ on which $f$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 02HY (lemma-lifting-along-artinian), implication (2) to (1). The square-zero condition in the definition of small extension is redundant and is made explicit for its subsequent use.

proof.text: Let $O$ be the union of all open subschemes $N\subseteq W$ for which $f|_N$ is smooth. Step 3 shows that $O$ contains every finite type point of $W$. The open-subset consequence of the finite type point lemma gives $O=|W|$. Thus these open subschemes cover $W$. Smoothness local on the source now implies that $f$ is smooth. If $W$ is empty the same conclusion follows from the empty-cover clause of that lemma.
